problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree and two different nodes of that tree, p and q. Return their lowest common ancestor: the deepest node that has both p and q as descendants, where a node counts as a descendant of itself. So if p is an ancestor of q, the answer is p.

problems.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree. Return the length of its diameter: the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes of the tree. The path may or may not pass through the root.

problems.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
problems.gist: You get the root of a binary tree. Imagine standing to the right of the tree and looking left. Return the values of the nodes you can see, listed from the top level to the bottom level. On each level you see exactly one node: the rightmost node of that level.

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.gist: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each consecutive pair is joined by an edge, and no node appears more than once. A path has at least one node and does not have to pass through the root. The path sum is the sum of the node values on it.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.gist: A company's reporting chart is stored as a binary tree: every manager has at most two direct reports, a left one and a right one. Each node holds an employee badge number val. You are given the root of the tree.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problems.gist: A ranking service keeps its scores in a BST: at every node, the whole left subtree holds smaller values and the whole right subtree holds larger ones.

problems.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree. Return the values of its nodes level by level, where the reading direction alternates: the first level (the root) is read left to right, the second level right to left, the third left to right again, and so on.

problems.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
problems.gist: A tree was lost, but two walks of it were logged as integer arrays of equal length. preorder lists the nodes in root, left subtree, right subtree order; inorder lists the same nodes in left subtree, root, right subtree order.

problems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.gist: An org chart is stored as a binary tree and you hold its root. Report how many levels the chart has: count the nodes on the deepest chain that starts at the top and ends at a leaf (a node with no children). A chart with no nodes at all has 0 levels.

problems.title: Symmetric Tree
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree that models a hanging mobile: each node carries a weight value.

problems.title: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree. Place the root at position (row 0, col 0). For a node at (row, col), its left child sits at (row + 1, col - 1) and its right child at (row + 1, col + 1).

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree. Invert it: for every node, exchange its left and right subtrees, so the result is the mirror image of the input. Return the root of the inverted tree (inverting in place and returning the same root object is fine).

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree

gfg.t: Lowest Common Ancestor in a BST

problems.gist: You get the root of a binary search tree and two nodes p and q that are both in the tree. Return their lowest common ancestor: the deepest node that has both p and q in its subtree. A node counts as a descendant of itself, so if p is an ancestor of q, the answer is p.

problems.title: Same Tree
problems.gist: You get the roots p and q of two binary trees. Return true if the two trees are identical: they have the same structure and every pair of nodes in the same position holds the same value. Otherwise return false.

problems.title: Balanced Binary Tree
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree that describes a company's reporting chart. Decide whether the chart is height-balanced: for every node, the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by no more than 1. Return true if so, false otherwise.

problems.title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree in which every node holds a single digit from 0 to 9.

problems.title: Binary Tree Vertical Order Traversal
problems.gist: You are given the root of a binary tree. Give the root column 0; a left child is one column to the left of its parent (col - 1) and a right child one column to the right (col + 1).
